newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa mostly down despite sterling.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa mostly down despite sterling.

text.p: London cocoa futures were mostly lower by midsession on light fund and trade selling despite slightly weaker sterling against the dollar.
But traders said the slide was halted by persistent scale-down industry buying at the lows.
"The market is slightly down when it should be up on sterling's comeback," said one trader.
But excluding crosses, volume at 1,185 lots was small in slow post-New Year holiday trade.
By the end of the morning trade, benchmark March was six stg down at 884 stg a tonne after re-testing a crucial 880 support.
A further chart support is seen at 878 stg, the lows seen on Monday. On the upside, resistance is pegged at 920.
Technically, analysts said they were looking for an upward correction to the oversold situation, with the market rising initially to 900-910 area.
Fundamentally, traders said pending significant supply/demand news, the market direction would hinge on sterling movement in the short-term.
Cocoa arrivals from top grower Ivory Coast are expected to pick up in January after the recent end to the rainy spell.
